#### 1. Seckel syndrome 8  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.666)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2939)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss of function mutation in DNA2 —DISRUPTS→ DNA2 (HGNC:2939); DNA2 (HGNC:2939) —DISRUPTS→ DNA replication and repair; DNA replication and repair —LEADS_TO→ Accumulation of DNA damage; Accumulation of DNA damage —LEADS_TO→ Chromosomal instability; Chromosomal instability —LEADS_TO→ Cell cycle arrest; Cell cycle arrest —LEADS_TO→ Apoptosis; Apoptosis —LEADS_TO→ Developmental defects; Developmental defects —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly; Developmental defects —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability; Developmental defects —LEADS_TO→ Seckel syndrome phenotype. Loss-of-function mutations in DNA2 disrupt its role in DNA replication and repair, leading to an accumulation of DNA damage and chromosomal instability. This instability triggers cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, particularly affecting rapidly dividing cells during development, resulting in the overlapping phenotypes of microcephaly, intellectual disability, and other developmental defects characteristic of both MONDO:0014062 and Seckel syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in DNA2 in patients with MONDO:0014062 or Seckel syndrome 8 that exhibits a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, rather than loss-of-function. _(variant: None)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared DNA2 mechanism could allow for the development of therapeutic strategies targeting DNA repair pathways or mitigating DNA damage accumulation, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.
